title: What are you doing this week?
content_html:
Rewriting the VM for Ekto---my little, typed, embeddable language that's a mixture of Koka, Lua, and Erlang.

One key thesis of Ekto is that algebraic effects are a good type formalism for talking about host-client interop in embedded scripting languages. I'm taking huge inspiration from Koka here and had been steadfastly committed to supporting multishot resumptions.

These are cool, they let you directly encode things like backtracking parsers or probabilistic programming as an effect. They're also very uncool because they make resource management a total headache. A resumption captures "the rest of the program" up until where the effect is handled and, more or less, that entire thing needs to be, in Rust terms, Clone at least.

There are ways around this, but they're all pretty unsatisfying. After chatting with some folks at Systems Distributed a few months ago I'd finally convinced myself to try just dropping multishot and using an effect system closer to OCaml 5: it's a runtime error to use a continuation twice.

That's really unsatisfying in it's own way. I feel like I'm still mourning this a bit. At the same time, single shot resumptions using a segmented stack are pretty nice and benefit a ton from an interpreted bytecode VM. I'm coming around to it being the right tradeoff. But, again, mourning a bit.
